THE MOVING BLOCKS AND TROLLS IN THE LEVELS

So basically, for the first bit with all the trolls. Although the first bit (where there's a huge row of spikes above you and the real exit is through the top) may seem like one level, in the code it's actually three different levels, which is why I've name the variable Fakelevel. 
This is quite confusing at the start but it will get easier, I promise!
[    ] So the first level seems like you have to go all the way to the   
       right. But when you do, a spike shoots out and you get killed. 
       [    ] What's actually happening is that your cube touches a hitbox 
              just before the edge. When that hitbox is activated, it 
              changes the Fakelevel variable by one, and also makes that 
              spike shoot out. 
       [    ] For the ground code, in a regular generic platformer there 
              will be a code that will look similar to:

[When green flag clicked]
[forever ]
[   ][switch costume to (level) ]
[______]

              What this essentially does is that when you touch the edge, 
              it's the next level, and then the ground costume will switch to 
              the next costume, which is the next set of platforms to move 
              on. But in this game, even though the Fakelevel has 
              changed to make the spike shoot out, we want the ground to 
              be the same as before so that:
              - it looks like you died from the spike and restarted the level
              - but in the actual code it thinks there is a new level
             So how do we do this? The answer is simple: create duplicate 
             costumes of the ground.
So:

At the start, the level is 1 and the costume being shown is also 1.

[Fakelevel [  1  ] ]
______________
|    __       __       |
|    |   |___|   |      |
|    |_______|      |
|                          |
|_____________|
|    costume1      |
-----------------------

But after you hit the hitbox, the level is 2 and the costume is 2. But we don't want the stage change, rather, we want it to look the exact same. So:

[Fakelevel [  2  ] ]
______________
|    __       __       |
|    |   |___|   |      |
|    |_______|      |
|                          |
|_____________|
|    costume2      |
-----------------------

Now, we can have the spike shoot out and make you die! 

If we did not do this, once we touch the hitbox it would have killed us, but still transported us to the next stage, and we do not want that.

And that brings us to an end of a tutorial to moving blocks in platformers!

___________

HOW TO MAKE THE CUBE GO BACKWARDS IN LEVELS

This is a very similar concept to the one used above, with the level number and the duplicating costumes. If we want to make us go from level 1 to 2, then 3, then 4, then backwards to 3, then back to 2, this is a very easy way to do it.

Lay out your costumes like this:
______________
|    __       __       |
|    |   |___|   |      |
|    |_______|      |
|                          |
|_____________|
|    costume1      |
-----------------------
______________
|    ________      |
|    |              |      |
|    |_______|      |
|                          |
|_____________|
|    costume2      |
-----------------------
______________
|                          |
|    ________      |
|    |__      __|      |
|         |__|           |
|_____________|
|    costume3      |
-----------------------
______________
|     __                 |
|    |__|  __          |
|           |__|         |
|                          |
|_____________|
|    costume4      |
-----------------------
______________
|     __                 |
|    |__|  __          |
|           |__|         |
|                          |
|_____________|
|    costume5      |
-----------------------
______________
|                          |
|    ________      |
|    |__      __|      |
|         |__|           |
|_____________|
|    costume6      |
-----------------------
______________
|    ________      |
|    |              |      |
|    |_______|      |
|                          |
|_____________|
|    costume7      |
-----------------------

Now, for levels one to four, we would put the next level hitbox on the right side of the screen. But after level 4, we want to make it so we have to go backwards. So once we hit the level 4 hitbox, we make sure that our costume 5 is the same as costume 4, so it looks like nothing has changed. But in levels 5 to 7, we want the hitbox to be on the left side of the screen. So once we hit the left of costume 5, which is identical to costume 4, we get transported into costume 6, which is identical to costume 3. Now repeat the process until you've moved back however many levels you want. Easy!
